hero.title: A small CMS layer for static Astro websites.

architecture.title: Your Astro website stays an Astro website.
architecture.lead: You describe the content in TypeScript. Mica gives editors forms for it and saves their work as files in Git. Astro reads the files through Content Collections and builds the static site. Mica looks after the content, and Astro serves the website.

benefits.title: Less between your content and your website.

items.title: No database, no CMS at runtime
items.text: Your website builds from files in Git. There is no content database to run, no content API to call, and no CMS service that your pages wait for.

items.title: Made for Astro
items.text: One TypeScript model gives the editor its forms and Astro its Content Collections, with types and validation. Fields go to JSON, rich text to Markdoc.

items.title: Your repository, your deploys
items.text: Content has a history that you can read and review. Publish makes a commit, and your build and your hosting stay as they are.

items.title: One collection at a time
items.text: Start a new Astro site with Mica, or add it to an existing one. Move the collections that people edit, and keep the others in Astro.

start.title: Start with your coding agent, or by hand.
start.text: Set up a new Astro site with Mica, or add Mica to a site that you have. A coding agent reads the setup guide, asks about your content and shows you a plan before it changes anything. Or install Mica by hand.

paths.label: Install by hand
paths.instruction: Run these commands in a terminal, in your Astro project.
paths.content:
# 1) Install the Mica packages
npm install @micacms/astro @micacms/core

# 2) Describe your content model; see https://micacms.com/docs/content-model/

# 3) Start the local Mica editor, with the live preview
npx @micacms/editor start --preview

preview.title: Edit content. See the result. Publish when ready.
preview.lead: Mica turns the model into forms for text, structured data, rich text and media. The form saves drafts by itself, and the real Astro page beside it shows them a second after you stop typing. Click a heading, a paragraph or an image on the page, and the cursor goes to its field. Publish puts the changes you choose on the website.

image.alt: The Mica editor with the form of the Services page on the left and the live preview of the page on the right. The page heading has an outline and the label Title, and the changed introduction has a dashed outline.

points.text: Your templates stay as they are: one line in astro.config
Changes that are not published yet have an outline of their own
Local: beside astro dev. Self-hosted: with an optional preview container
Forms beside the page, not a page builder

run.title: On your laptop while you build. On your server for your team.
run.lead: Both edit the same files in the same repository, and the website depends on neither. The choice is who edits, and where the editor runs.

options.title: Local editor
options.text: Runs on your machine, on your Git checkout, beside astro dev with the live preview. Only your machine can reach it. Publish commits and pushes with your own Git credentials.

needs.text: A Git repository, and Git LFS if you use it
No sign-in, no account, no database

options.title: Self-hosted editor
options.text: A container on your server. Editors sign in through your identity provider, for example Google. Mica keeps its own Git clone on a volume, with Git LFS built in. An optional second container gives the live preview.

needs.text: A server with Docker Compose and one volume
A token that can push to the repository
For the live preview: the preview container and a second host name

agents.title: Your agent edits too. It saves drafts, like everybody else.
agents.lead: Mica has an MCP server built in. Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or any other MCP client can read your content model and change your content, with the same checks as the editor. You do not need an agent to use Mica.

points.text: Reads the content model, and Mica checks every value
Saves drafts. Publishing by an agent is off, unless you turn it on
Sends the revision it read, so it never overwrites a newer save
Works with the local and the self-hosted editor

capabilities.title: Enough for real content.
capabilities.lead: The parts that are hard to keep in order without a CMS: links between entries, many media files, and content apart from the code.

items.title: Fields for structured content, with relations
items.text: Each field has a label and rules, and Mica checks every value. Relations link entries across collections, such as an article to its author or a project to its team, and also to the items of a JSON or CSV file. When an entry gets a new URL, Mica offers to update the links to it.

items.title: Images and files, also in Git LFS
items.text: An image can require alt text. Editors drop a whole set of photos on a field, and GPX, PDF or CSV files go next to them. Git LFS keeps large files out of your normal Git history.

items.title: Content apart from the code
items.text: Put the content in a repository of its own, as a Git submodule, so that content and presentation stay apart. Editors publish there, and Mica never commits in the website's repository.

fit.title: Small on purpose.
fit.lead: Mica is for content-driven Astro websites whose owners want static builds and Git as the source of truth. It is experimental and not ready for production. Here is what it does not do, so that you can choose well.

good.text: A content-driven Astro website: a company site, a blog, documentation
One developer, and two to five people who write
Content in Git, as files that people can read
A static website with no CMS code in it

not.text: Roles or approval steps inside the editor
A page builder, or typing text directly into the page
A 1.0 promise: the API and the content format can still change

cta.title: Add content editing without replacing Astro.
cta.text: Try Mica on your laptop, with a new or an existing Astro site. Put the editor on your server when other people need it in their browser.
